newsitem.title: USA: NCAA- BASKETBALL-ARIZONA, NORTH CAROLINA CLINCH LAST FINAL FOUR BERTHS.
newsitem.headline: NCAA- BASKETBALL-ARIZONA, NORTH CAROLINA CLINCH LAST FINAL FOUR BERTHS.

text.p: Fourth seeds Arizona ended the Cinderella run of 10th-seeded Providence with an overtime victory in the Southeast Region final Sunday to join three top-seeded teams in the NCAA men's basketball tournament Final Four.

Providence, the only double digit seed to reach the round of eight, erased a 10-point deficit late in the second half but missed a chance to win in the closing seonds of regulation and Arizona (23-9) pulled out a 96-92 overtime victory.

Miles Simon scored a career-high 30 points for Arizona. His eight-foot runner with 2:54 to play in overtime snapped a tie and propelled his team to the national semifinals in Indianapolis next Saturday.
Arizona, which played giant killer by knocking out pre-tournament favourite top-ranked Kansas in the previous round, will face North Carolina in one Final Four matchup.
Dean Smith reached his 11th Final Four as coach of North Carolina when his Tar Heels whipped sixth-seeded Louisville 97-74 in the East Region final at Syracuse, New York.
Defending champions Kentucky, which won the West region, and Midwest region winner Minnesota nailed down the first two Final Four spots Saturday.
In Birmingham, God Shammgod and Jamel Thomas scored 23 points apiece for Providence (24-12), which had upset second-seeded Duke in the second round.
Thomas forced overtime and capped a comeback helped by Arizona mistakes when he hit a three-pointer from the left baseline with 15.3 seconds left.

Arizona then turned over the ball, but a three-point attempt by Corey Wright in the final seconds of regulation was off the mark and ultimately cost the Providence its first Final Four appearance since 1987.
After Simon's big basket, Jason Terry hit a 15-footer to give Arizona a four-point lead with 64 seconds left and a Simon free throw gave the Wildcats a safe five-point cushion.
Mike Bibby had 17 points, Bennett Davison added 14 and 12 rebounds for Arizona.
Derrick Brown chipped in 18 points and Ruben Garces added 16 points and 19 rebounds for Providence, which was without its best shooter at crunch time after Austin Croshere fouled out with 9:16 left.

In the East, Shammond Williams scored 22 points and Vince Carter had five points in a key second-half run as North Carolina squandered most of a 21-point halftime lead before running away for a 23-point victory.
Carter finished with 15 points for the Tar Heels (28-6), who had all five starters score in double figures and extended their winning streak to 16 games.

Smith, who passed legendary Kentucky coach Adolph Rupp to move atop the all-time college basketball wins list in the second round, will be looking for his third National title in his fourth trip to the Final Four this decade.
Alex Sanders scored 20 points and Alvin Sims added 14 for Louisville, which was in the regional finals for the first time since winning the national title in 1986.
Williams scored 15 of his points in the first half as North Carolina stormed to a 54-33 halftime lead.

The Cardinals, with starting point guard DeJuan Wheat playing on a badly sprained left ankle, made a run at the Tar Heels in the second half using bursts of 7-1 and 8-0 to pull within seven points at 59-52 with 13:29 left.
B.J. Flynn hit two three-pointers to cap a 9-3 run for Louisville, and with 8:14 to go the Cardinals were down by just one three-pointer at 69-66.
But the Cardinals went cold, missing on nine consecutive shots as North Carolina pulled away for the victory.
"One thing about this team is there's no quit in them," said longtime Louisville coach Denny Crum.
"I think that second half run showed the kind of character that they have, and they've done that all year. I know we kind of ran out of gas, but we made a great run at them."
